generated.what_happened: A study led by Stanford Medicine researchers has revealed that the brain is not a single contiguous organ, but rather two distinct neural systems that evolved independently and merged over 550 million years of evolution. By analyzing embryonic development in mice, the team discovered that the forebrain and midbrain arise from a completely separate progenitor cell population than the hindbrain. This fundamental developmental split explains past difficulties in growing rear brain cells in laboratories and enabled the researchers to successfully cultivate functional human hindbrain neurons from stem cells for the first time. The breakthrough offers new opportunities to study automatic functions and develop treatments for devastating brain stem diseases such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and spinal muscular atrophy.
